slot.brief: PV diagram of a closed cycle (rectangle or triangle) given; ask for net work done over the cycle by computing the enclosed area; figure shows the cycle.

stem: For the closed $P$–$V$ cycle shown in the figure, find the net work done by the gas in one cycle.

verdicts.working: The cycle is clockwise, so the net work is the enclosed area: $(3\times10^{-3})(3\times10^5-1\times10^5)=600\,\text{J}$.

working:
$W_{\text{net}}=\text{area enclosed}=\Delta P\,\Delta V$
$=(3-1)\times10^5(5-2)\times10^{-3}=600\ \text{J}$
$\text{Clockwise cycle}\Rightarrow W_{\text{net}}>0$

Independent check: The cycle is clockwise, so the net work is the enclosed area: $(3\times10^{-3})(3\times10^5-1\times10^5)=600\,\text{J}$.
solution:
For a clockwise cycle, the net work done by the gas equals the positive area enclosed in the $P$–$V$ diagram.
$$W_{\text{net}}=(3-1)\times10^5(5-2)\times10^{-3}=600\ \text{J}$$

Add arrows along the path from the lower-left corner upward to the upper-left corner, rightward to the upper-right corner, downward to the lower-right corner, and leftward back to the lower-left corner.
